.qc-cache/kittle-2026-10-09-r2/rules/harbor-webdev-rubric-qc/references/staged-task-contract.md :: scoring.toml section (lines 83-96), test.sh section (lines 102-111), tools section (162-164)
evidence: Policy: task/tests/scoring.toml is byte-identical to the frozen template (sha256 95f70d6e...bbba both): [gates] render = 0.0, constraints = 0.0; [weights] functional 0.6 / polish 0.2 / visual 0.2; [floors] functional = 0.05. task/tests/tools/score.py is byte-identical to the template (sha256 13de2b38...c04e) and task/tests/test.sh is identical to the template test.sh (diff empty). Gates carry no mass: score.py:46 computes weighted only over [weights] (functional/polish/visual); gate dimensions are only used as pass/fail at score.py:41 (scores[k] > 0.0). Both gate judge.toml files use aggregation = "all_pass" with one type = "binary" criterion (render: authenticated_render; constraints: server_backed_local_application, which posts JUDGE-G1, reloads and reads it back as harriet in a separate context, so a static/dead shell fails). Gate-before-shaping ordering: test.sh:212-222 removes any old scored dir, runs the gates suite (a rewardkit failure exits with the pre-written zero reward from write_zero_reward at test.sh:60), then score.py; exit 1 (gate failed) -> exit 0 before run_suite scored (test.sh:224), so the scored suite is skipped; any other error -> write_zero_reward. score.py:42 additionally requires gates_passed before reading scored data and :48 zeroes reward unless gates_passed and floors_passed. Local execution of the frozen score.py+scoring.toml on synthetic suite outputs (scratchpad r43, python -I): render=0 with perfect scored -> reward 0.0, exit 1; constraints=0 -> reward 0.0, exit 1; gates pass but no scored reward.json -> reward 0.0; functional=0.0 with polish=visual=1 -> reward 0.0 (weighted 0.4 withheld, floors_passed 0); functional=0.04545 (one 1.5-weight criterion of 33) -> reward 0.0; functional=0.0606 (one 2.0 criterion) -> 0.4364; functional-only perfect -> 0.6; all perfect -> 1.0. Floor arithmetic for this task: functional weights sum to 33.0 (2,2,2,2,1.5,3,2,2,2,2,1.5,2,2.5,2,2.5,2), so clearing 0.05 requires >1.65 weight, i.e. at least one fully passed 2.0+ functional criterion, each of which is a multi-part server-enforced behaviour (e.g. signin_and_client_scope needs client scoping, sign-out wipe, signed-out replay refusal and cross-matter replay refusal; persistence needs a real restart). An app whose functional behaviour is broken earns 0 regardless of polish/visual. Polish and visual prompts also restate the in-dimension browser gate that zeroes a static shell/facade. Broken-app attempt: a gate-passing chat with no working features gets functional 0 -> reward 0. Conforming-alternative attempt: a correct app cannot be zeroed by gates beyond sign-in/post/reload/cross-user readback, all of which the brief requires. Residual risk: these are source checks plus a local score.py execution; raw-evidence-index.json states full configured grading, reward discrimination/ranking and Oracle scores are absent, so the end-to-end test.sh gate-fail path (scored suite actually skipped inside the verifier) has not been measured. Note (not a defect, template-controlled): a basic membership-scoped chat that fully passes one 2.0 functional criterion clears the floor and could then collect sign-in/phone-width polish and sidebar/phone visual points (roughly 0.15-0.2 total by my estimate); the 0.05 floor is frozen template policy and such an app is partially working, not non-working.
